body.statement: Assume \(s=\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\). Determine whether the proved bracket can be sharpened to \(\rho_\star(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\) over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Any converse must use priors on observed laws in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) whose full-law null lifts in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}\) each have constant \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\) and exact \(X\sim\lambda\), while preserving all separate Hölder restrictions. Determine whether the sharp rough-regime rate depends on \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) separately and whether logarithms occur at any additional boundary or interior elbow within this strict regime. The equality case \(s=2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\) is excluded: the observational-rate-bracket theorem already proves \(\rho_\star(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\) there without a logarithmic loss.

obligation.what_is_open: For \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), whether the nuisance-limited upper endpoint \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\) is the full-class minimax separation rate, and whether any further rough-regime elbow carries a logarithmic factor.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle Bernoulli bump mixture proves only the oracle lower endpoint. A nuisance-scale converse requires a prior whose every null draw has constant CATE, whose alternatives satisfy the separate propensity, baseline, and CATE Hölder restrictions, and whose complete four-cell observed likelihood remains close under exact uniform design. The available correlated propensity--baseline perturbation does not control all transition regions and can force the alternative baseline to inherit impermissible CATE roughness when \(\beta>\gamma\).
obligation.attempted: The corrected projection upper bound was audited for unrelated ranks, including regimes with both ranks larger than \(n\), and the oracle sign-mixture lower bound was completed. A local moment-matched propensity--baseline perturbation was not promoted because it neither matches the full observed Bernoulli cell likelihood nor bounds the fixed-design transition-region contribution.
obligation.partial_result:
The observational-rate-bracket theorem gives the complete proved result
\[
 c_{\mathrm{rate}}n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}
 \le \rho_\star(n)
 \le C_{\mathrm{rate}}\left\{
 n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\vee
 n^{-4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)/[4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)+d(\alpha+\beta)+2d\gamma]}
 \right\}.
\]
For the lower inequality, every observed-data test is also a known-propensity test that ignores its propensity input, so the known-propensity minimax radius is no larger than \(\rho_\star(n)\); the known-propensity benchmark then gives the displayed lower endpoint.  For the upper inequality, the computable-upper-bound theorem supplies the terminating corrected-energy test uniformly over the same observed-law class.  Writing \(s=\alpha+\beta\), comparison of the two positive exponents gives
\[
 \frac{4\gamma s}{4\gamma s+ds+2d\gamma}
 \ge \frac{2\gamma}{4\gamma+d}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 s(4\gamma+d)\ge 2d\gamma.
\]
Hence the endpoints match when \(s\ge 2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), including equality, where the two exact power sequences coincide and no logarithmic loss is present.  In the strict complementary regime the proved upper endpoint is \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\), but no matching legal same-class observational converse has been established.

body.justification: This question is now confined to deciding whether the proved nuisance-limited upper endpoint is sharp below the no-penalty boundary.
body.gap: No legal same-class composite-null mixture currently attains the nuisance scale while preserving exact uniform design and all three separate Hölder restrictions.
body.consumer: A resolution would sharpen the existing bracket only in the strict rough regime and determine any further rate elbows or logarithmic factors there.
